etymologies.etymologyHTML: From clock +‎ -wise.

definitions.definition: In a curve or twist corresponding to the movement of the hands of a clock.

quote.citation: 2009 May 28, Alan Feuer, “In the Gilded World of Per Se’s Kitchen”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: The main — or cooking — kitchen is an inhumanly immaculate expanse of burner rings and countertops where, according to tradition, the stations move clockwise from canapé to entremetier.

definitions.definition: Moving clockwise; having rotary motion in the manner of a clock.

quote.text: The clockwise beating of cilia results in a net flow of extraembryonic fluid leftwards  […]
